mechanism_inventory: stale accounting snapshot — margin updated before callTradeAfterCallback; a reentering call sees the partially-updated vault state

missing invariant enforcement — checkSafe is called after the external callback, so a callback that manipulates vault margin after the fee/payoff credit but before the safety check could leave the vault undercollateralized without triggering revert

hook caller or hook-timing mismatch — msg.sender is trusted as the hook (IHooks(msg.sender)) without any whitelist/registry check visible in this source, allowing any caller to supply a malicious hook implementation

wrong lifecycle ordering — initializeLock is called inside callTradeAfterCallback, which is called from trade after margin is already credited; the lock does not cover the Trade.trade call where settlement occurs, leaving a window

victim accounting direction — marginAmountUpdate is added unconditionally to vault margin after finalizeLock; if finalizeLock can be made to return a favorable (positive) marginAmountUpdate without actual token settlement, the caller gains margin for free

access-control mismatch — the callTradeAfterCallback is internal and invokes msg.sender as the hook; the outer trade() is external; anyone can call trade() and supply themselves as the hook callback target
external-call failure / DoS — IHooks(msg.sender).predyTradeAfterCallback could revert or consume all gas, bricking the trade for a victim vault

precision / packing / normalization edge — tradeResult.fee + tradeResult.payoff.perpPayoff + tradeResult.payoff.sqrtPayoff are summed as int256 before being added to margin; signed overflow or incorrect sign conventions could corrupt vault margin

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: msg.sender is cast unconditionally to IHooks without any authorization check visible in the source. Any EOA or contract that calls trade() becomes the hook and has full control over predyTradeAfterCallback, which is invoked after vault margin has already been modified with fee/payoff credits. The malicious hook can re-enter trade() or manipulate global state inside the callback window.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Unprivileged: any contract that implements predyTradeAfterCallback deploys and calls trade() directly on PredyPool. No role or allowance required from the source as shown.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker deploys MaliciousHook implementing IHooks. 2. Attacker calls PredyPool.trade() with a crafted TradeParams. 3. Inside trade(), margin is credited with fee+payoffs, then callTradeAfterCallback is entered. 4. initializeLock sets a lock state. 5. IHooks(msg.sender) resolves to MaliciousHook.predyTradeAfterCallback. 6. Inside the callback, attacker calls trade() again (or another PredyPool entry) to manipulate vault state or drain funds before finalizeLock enforces the BaseTokenNotSettled check. 7. finalizeLock runs on the outer call; if the inner call already settled/consumed base token the outer check may pass or the state is corrupted.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol LPs / other vault owners lose funds; protocol solvency invariant broken.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker gains margin credits or extracted tokens.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: The hook trust assumption is the central architectural issue: no source fact proves msg.sender is restricted to registered/whitelisted hooks. The callback fires after margin mutation and before checkSafe, creating the highest-severity window.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: checkSafe is called AFTER the external callback callTradeAfterCallback. The callback credits marginAmountUpdate to the vault unconditionally once finalizeLock returns a non-zero int256. If the callback can produce a large positive marginAmountUpdate (by manipulating token flows inside the lock), the vault could show a margin surplus that is not backed by real tokens, inflating apparent solvency.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Unprivileged caller controlling predyTradeAfterCallback (same as above) or a legitimate but adversarial settlement path.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker's callback arranges for finalizeLock to return a large positive marginAmountUpdate (e.g., by moving tokens in a way the lock accounting misattributes). 2. globalData.vaults[vaultId].margin is inflated by that amount. 3. checkSafe then runs on an inflated margin and passes. 4. Attacker subsequently withdraws the inflated margin or opens larger positions backed by phantom margin.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol and LPs whose funds back vault solvency.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Affects a different accounting variable (marginAmountUpdate post-callback vs fee/payoff pre-callback) and a different timing window. The ordering of checkSafe after external call is the source locus.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: Wrong lifecycle ordering — Trade.trade() executes settlement (including external ISettlement calls) before initializeLock is called inside callTradeAfterCallback. The lock therefore does not protect the settlement phase. Whether ISettlement is user-supplied or restricted is not shown in this source.
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: Trade.trade(globalData, tradeParams, settlementData) is called at line 198 before callTradeAfterCallback (line 208) and before initializeLock (line 229). settlementData is a bytes parameter passed in from the caller.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Is ISettlement user-supplied or restricted to a whitelist? If user-supplied, the settlement callback executes outside the lock window and could manipulate pool state before margin is written.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol / other vault owners if settlement is exploitable outside the lock.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker who controls the settlement address embedded in settlementData.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: Signed integer overflow or sign-convention error in margin computation: tradeResult.fee + tradeResult.payoff.perpPayoff + tradeResult.payoff.sqrtPayoff are summed as int256 and added to margin. If any component has an unexpected sign (e.g., fee is negative in a losing trade but is added rather than subtracted), margin could be incorrectly inflated or deflated.
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: Line 200-201: globalData.vaults[tradeParams.vaultId].margin += tradeResult.fee + tradeResult.payoff.perpPayoff + tradeResult.payoff.sqrtPayoff. All three are int256; sign conventions are defined in Trade/Perp libraries not shown.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Are the signs of fee, perpPayoff, sqrtPayoff consistent with the += direction? A systematic sign flip would silently corrupt vault margin.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol (if attacker's vault margin is inflated) or the trader (if own margin is incorrectly debited).
unresolved_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker or protocol depending on sign direction.

rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: A reverting callback would cause the entire trade() call to revert, which is a self-inflicted or griefing DoS at most. The caller (msg.sender) is the hook; if the caller's own hook reverts, only the caller's transaction fails. No third-party vault is affected unless a shared state lock is left in a bad state — but initializeLock/finalizeLock are in the same call frame and would revert together.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: The revert unwinds all state changes including the lock. No permanent lock-in of bad state results from a simple revert in this call frame.

impact_direction.attacker_receives: Vault margin credits or extracted protocol tokens via manipulated hook callback or inflated marginAmountUpdate.
impact_direction.attacker_preserves: Control over vault after safety check passes on inflated state.
impact_direction.victim_loses: Protocol LPs lose funds backing vault solvency; other vaults may be affected by corrupted global accounting.
impact_direction.invariant_violated: Vault solvency invariant: checkSafe must pass on honestly-computed margin. The ordering of external callback before checkSafe, combined with unchecked msg.sender-as-hook, allows margin to be manipulated between the pre-callback credit and the post-callback safety check.
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: The exploit requires no privileged role and no admin precondition. The attacker deploys a contract and calls trade() — permissionless entry. Impact is not dust: vault margin corruption or fund extraction scales with vault size.
